dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: You keep treating every disagreement like a puzzle. Could you tell me what you actually think?

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: I'm curious too. Not a theory this time, just your view.

dialogue.speaker: Jules
dialogue.text: I thought Owen was talking about the train station.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: No, I meant the old ferry landing. My mistake for not saying it clearly.

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: I'm still thinking about what I said earlier.

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: Take your time. We don't have to fill the quiet.

dialogue.speaker: Allen
dialogue.text: Did we ever decide where that bridge in the photo was?

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: We didn't. Someone suggested the coast, but we never verified it.

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: We have probably exhausted this discussion of bus timetables.

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: Fine by me. I'd rather talk about something we're actually curious about.

dialogue.speaker: Jules
dialogue.text: Maybe the whole problem is that we keep talking in circles about talking in circles.

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: Exactly, talking in circles about talking in circles is getting old.

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: I think the map is outdated.

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: No, it shows the new bridge. The date is printed at the bottom.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: Jules, did you look at the rainfall graph?

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: I only saw yesterday's summary.

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: I left the blue notebook on the window ledge.

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: The one with the pressed leaf inside?

dialogue.speaker: Allen
dialogue.text: Sarah, what would distinguish a real clue from a coincidence here?

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: We could compare independent observations.

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: You said the sculpture was made in 1920, right?

dialogue.speaker: Jules
dialogue.text: I don't remember anyone verifying its date.

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: I thought the door was locked.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: I just checked it. The handle turns and the door opens.

dialogue.speaker: Allen
dialogue.text: Can anyone explain why the shore is brighter than the lake?

dialogue.speaker: Jules
dialogue.text: I've only been watching the clouds.

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: It bothered me that nobody answered my question about the photo.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: I missed it. Could you tell us which part?

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: The missing book was on the second shelf.

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: Good, that settles where it went.

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: I heard a strange metallic ring from the hallway.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: Was it before or after the elevator moved?

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: Mara, what made you change your view of the sculpture?

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: Give me a second, I'm thinking.

dialogue.speaker: Jules
dialogue.text: I said three people, not thirteen.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: That does change the estimate quite a bit.

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: Did we actually see a bird land, or only hear wings?

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: I only heard wings; I never saw the bird.

dialogue.speaker: Jules
dialogue.text: I finally found the sketch I lost last week.

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: What part of it was so difficult to replace?
